title: Nonnegative binary rational hafnians: an exact reduction and approximation and sampling consequences
seo_title: Nonnegative rational hafnians and perfect matchings | Alec Kriebel
meta_description: An attributed exact reduction of binary rational hafnians to unweighted perfect matchings, with polynomial bit bounds and quantitative approximate sampling.
abstract: We give a self-contained implementation of classical positive-integer weight removal for perfect matchings. A binary directed acyclic graph with W paths gives a simple two-terminal graph with matching signature (W,1,0,0) using 4 bits(W)−2 vertices. Gluing these gadgets and clearing denominators reduces every nonnegative binary rational hafnian to an unweighted simple-graph perfect-matching count with polynomial encoding length. Consequently, the general-graph FPRAS of OpenAI gives a uniform FPRAS for this rational model, with exact zero detection. We specify a bounded-bit counting self-reduction sampler with explicit total-variation and runtime bounds. The approximation breakthrough, logarithmic weight removal, and count-to-sample framework are inherited; this note supplies explicit proofs, bit bounds, boundary cases, and reproducible finite checks. Its approximation conclusions rely on the cited general-graph theorem and do not concern signed or complex hafnians.
